/-!
# Conjecture 1.31

by M. I. Kargapolov

Is a residually finite group with the maximum condition for subgroups almost polycyclic?

Here a group is *residually finite* if every non-identity element lies outside some
normal subgroup of finite index (equivalently, is mapped to a non-identity element by
some homomorphism to a finite group). A group satisfies the *maximum condition for
subgroups* (is a *Noetherian group*) if every non-empty set of subgroups has a maximal
element, i.e. every strictly ascending chain of subgroups is finite; equivalently, every
subgroup is finitely generated. A group is *polycyclic* if it has a subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$ with all factors
$G_{i+1}/G_i$ cyclic, and *almost* (= virtually) polycyclic if it has a polycyclic subgroup
of finite index.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

A group $G$ is *residually finite* if for every $g \in G$ with $g \neq 1$ there is a
normal subgroup $N \trianglelefteq G$ of finite index with $g \notin N$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.FiniteIndex / Subgroup.Normal (used as building blocks); no residual-finiteness predicate exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
justification.name: Kourovka.«1.31».IsResiduallyFinite
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a residually finite group (only a passing mention in a docstring of GroupTheory/Torsion.lean). Defined as: for every g ≠ 1 there is a normal subgroup of finite index not containing g.

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if for every $g \in G$ with $g \neq 1$ there is a
normal subgroup $N \trianglelefteq G$ of finite index with $g \notin N$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), s 0 = ⊥ ∧ s (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, s i.castSucc ≤ s i.succ ∧
      ∃ _ : ((s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ)).Normal,
        IsCyclic (s i.succ ⧸ (s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ))
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *polycyclic* if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$, i.e. a chain of
subgroups with $G_0$ trivial, $G_n = G$ and each $G_i$ normal in $G_{i+1}$, such that every
factor group $G_{i+1}/G_i$ is cyclic.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsSolvable / derivedSeries (solvable ≠ polycyclic in general), CompositionSeries/JordanHolderLattice (factors are required maximal-normal, not cyclic), IsCyclic + Subgroup.subgroupOf + QuotientGroup (used as building blocks).
justification.name: Kourovka.«1.31».IsPolycyclic
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no polycyclic groups and no subnormal series for subgroups. Defined literally as a finite chain ⊥ = s 0 ≤ … ≤ s (Fin.last n) = ⊤ with each s i normal in s (i+1) (via Subgroup.subgroupOf) and cyclic quotient (IsCyclic of the QuotientGroup).

blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is *polycyclic* if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$, i.e. a chain of
subgroups with $G_0$ trivial, $G_n = G$ and each $G_i$ normal in $G_{i+1}$, such that every
factor group $G_{i+1}/G_i$ is cyclic. -/
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), s 0 = ⊥ ∧ s (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, s i.castSucc ≤ s i.succ ∧
      ∃ _ : ((s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ)).Normal,
        IsCyclic (s i.succ ⧸ (s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ))

def IsVirtuallyPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ H : Subgroup G, IsPolycyclic H ∧ H.FiniteIndex
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *almost polycyclic* (or *virtually polycyclic*, or *polycyclic-by-finite*)

justification.name: Kourovka.«1.31».IsVirtuallyPolycyclic
justification.why_needed: 'Almost polycyclic' = has a polycyclic subgroup of finite index; no such predicate exists. Modelled on Mathlib's Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent (∃ N : Subgroup G, IsNilpotent N ∧ FiniteIndex N).

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question, implicitly universally quantified over all groups G: the Prop is `∀ G, (G residually finite) ∧ (G satisfies the maximal condition on subgroups, i.e. every subgroup is finitely generated / ACC on subgroups, 'Noetherian group') → G is almost (= virtually) polycyclic, i.e. has a polycyclic subgroup of finite index`; 'polycyclic' (subnormal series with cyclic factors) and 'residually finite' are not in Mathlib and would need helper definitions, and the quantification over groups must be handled with a universe-polymorphic `∀ (G : Type*) [Group G]` rather than a fixed type.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates compile and state the same mathematics: `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G], residually finite → maximum condition on subgroups → ∃ finite-index polycyclic subgroup`. Residual finiteness (c01–c07: a finite-index normal subgroup omits each g ≠ 1; c08: separation by a homomorphism to a finite group in `Type`) is standard and equivalent in both encodings. Polycyclic (subnormal series ⊥ = s 0 ≤ … ≤ s n = ⊤ with s i normal in s (i+1) and cyclic quotient; c07 uses the descending direction, c02 an elementwise cyclic-coset encoding) is correct in all; repeated terms / n = 0 are harmless (trivial factors are cyclic, trivial group is polycyclic). 'Almost polycyclic' = finite-index polycyclic subgroup in all. For the maximum condition, c01/c03/c05/c06 use `WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G)`, which I verified in a scratch file is exactly 'every nonempty family of subgroups has a maximal element' — the literal reading of the source — while c02/c04/c07/c08 use the (classically equivalent) `∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG`. I chose c05 for the literal `WellFoundedGT`, the clearest docstrings (recording the equivalences), and proven `@[category API]` sanity lemmas for the bespoke definitions as CONTRIBUTING.md requests. Verified: theorem is universe-polymorphic (`Type u_1`), the quotient's group instance uses the bound `Normal` witness, answer linter not triggered, no lines > 100 chars. Edit: docstrings slightly extended to mention the 'every subgroup finitely generated' equivalence.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 1.31

by M. I. Kargapolov

Is a residually finite group with the maximum condition for subgroups almost polycyclic?

Here a group is *residually finite* if every non-identity element lies outside some
normal subgroup of finite index (equivalently, is mapped to a non-identity element by
some homomorphism to a finite group). A group satisfies the *maximum condition for
subgroups* (is a *Noetherian group*) if every non-empty set of subgroups has a maximal
element, i.e. every strictly ascending chain of subgroups is finite; equivalently, every
subgroup is finitely generated. A group is *polycyclic* if it has a subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$ with all factors
$G_{i+1}/G_i$ cyclic, and *almost* (= virtually) polycyclic if it has a polycyclic subgroup
of finite index.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«1.31»

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if for every $g \in G$ with $g \neq 1$ there is a
normal subgroup $N \trianglelefteq G$ of finite index with $g \notin N$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- A group $G$ is *polycyclic* if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$, i.e. a chain of
subgroups with $G_0$ trivial, $G_n = G$ and each $G_i$ normal in $G_{i+1}$, such that every
factor group $G_{i+1}/G_i$ is cyclic. -/
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), s 0 = ⊥ ∧ s (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, s i.castSucc ≤ s i.succ ∧
      ∃ _ : ((s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ)).Normal,
        IsCyclic (s i.succ ⧸ (s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ))

/-- A group $G$ is *almost polycyclic* (or *virtually polycyclic*, or *polycyclic-by-finite*)
if it has a polycyclic subgroup of finite index. -/
def IsVirtuallyPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ H : Subgroup G, IsPolycyclic H ∧ H.FiniteIndex

/-- Every finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsResiduallyFinite.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/-- The trivial group is polycyclic. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsPolycyclic.of_subsingleton (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    IsPolycyclic G :=
  ⟨0, fun _ => ⊥, rfl, Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun i => i.elim0⟩

/-- Every cyclic group is polycyclic. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsPolycyclic.of_isCyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsCyclic G] : IsPolycyclic G := by
  refine ⟨1, ![⊥, ⊤], rfl, rfl, fun i => ?_⟩
  obtain rfl := Fin.fin_one_eq_zero i
  simp only [Fin.castSucc_zero, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Fin.succ_zero_eq_one, Matrix.cons_val_one,
    Subgroup.bot_subgroupOf]
  exact ⟨bot_le, inferInstance,
    isCyclic_of_surjective (QuotientGroup.mk' _) (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _)⟩

/-- Every finite group is almost polycyclic. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsVirtuallyPolycyclic.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsVirtuallyPolycyclic G :=
  ⟨⊥, IsPolycyclic.of_subsingleton _, inferInstance⟩

/--
Is a residually finite group with the maximum condition for subgroups almost polycyclic?

The maximum condition for subgroups (every non-empty set of subgroups of $G$ has a maximal
element, equivalently every ascending chain of subgroups of $G$ stabilises, equivalently
every subgroup of $G$ is finitely generated) is stated as `WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G)`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.31» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G], IsResiduallyFinite G → WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G) →
      IsVirtuallyPolycyclic G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.31»

items: Maximum condition for subgroups is encoded as `WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G)` (no infinite strictly ascending chain / every nonempty set of subgroups has a maximal element), rather than the equivalent 'every subgroup is finitely generated' (`∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG`). This matches Mathlib's `isNoetherian_iff'` encoding for modules.

Residual finiteness is defined via finite-index normal subgroups separating non-identity elements, rather than via homomorphisms to finite groups; the two are classically equivalent and the subgroup form avoids quantifying over a universe of finite groups.

`IsPolycyclic` requires the series to be an actual chain (`s i.castSucc ≤ s i.succ`) in addition to normality of `(s i).subgroupOf (s (i+1))` and cyclicity of the quotient; without the chain condition `subgroupOf` would silently intersect. The normality witness is bound as `∃ _ : (...).Normal, IsCyclic (...)` so the quotient carries its group structure; a series of length n = 0 is allowed (trivial group).

'Almost polycyclic' is read as 'virtually polycyclic' (has a polycyclic subgroup of finite index), the standard meaning in the Kourovka Notebook; since polycyclic groups are closed under finite-index overgroups modulo the finite quotient, this is the same as polycyclic-by-finite.
The quantification over groups is universe-polymorphic (`∀ (G : Type*) [Group G]`) as required by the decomposition table, unlike the other Kourovka files which use `Type`.

Three short `@[category API]` sanity lemmas were added (finite ⇒ residually finite; trivial and cyclic groups are polycyclic; finite ⇒ almost polycyclic) to test the bespoke definitions, following CONTRIBUTING.md's request for basic API tests.

reviewer_notes: Problem is a single yes/no question; the final statement is `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G], IsResiduallyFinite G → WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G) → IsVirtuallyPolycyclic G`, with `answer(True)` = positive answer. Bespoke definitions (IsResiduallyFinite, IsPolycyclic, IsVirtuallyPolycyclic) live in the problem file, as in Kourovka/1_40.lean; a repository PR might move them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/. Nobody omitted or objected to the slot; no candidate had a faithfulness defect — the choice among them is stylistic. Minor interpretive point: 'almost polycyclic' is read as 'has a polycyclic subgroup of finite index' (normality not required); this is equivalent to polycyclic-by-finite via the normal core. The file uses `Type*` (universe-polymorphic) per the decomposition notes, whereas existing Kourovka files use `Type`.
